output.summary: Require working sparse selection for a conventional Go module as well as Node/TypeScript, with explicit package/import coverage and safe fallback for unsupported constructs. The release gate includes real independent Go package targets and full-suite comparison.

Implementation re-review resolved both malformed-tree implementation and regression-test findings. No open findings or notes require verdicts.

Add versioned Go package dependency model and broaden the TypeScript model, with reusable raw import facts rebuilt from pinned bytes, revision-specific reverse closure and bounded package-and-dependent fallback for changed exact embedded inputs. All frozen suites passed (29 conservative, 11 coordinator, 3 installed package, 17 v2), plus eight model tests and build. Real Go execution passed the baseline; an intentional A regression failed selected A and consumer tests and the full suite while independent B passed. Scope is intentionally limited: Go cgo, external modules, build tags and unmodeled inputs fall back; Python and mixed-language dependencies remain unsupported. G2 must independently validate the new exact model versions, runtime requirements and bounded package scopes before any sparse execution. Windows ACL host validation remains outstanding.

findings.impact: The project could pass its release gates while reproducing the Node-only admission the owner rejected.
findings.text: The acceptance requirement for two-target sparse plans applies only to each demonstrably supported slice, but does not require any non-Node slice to be supported. Python and Go fixtures could always fall back to the full profile while only Node demonstrates selection, leaving the owner-requested multilingual impact capability unproven. Name a minimum supported set and require a real sparse case in at least one non-Node ecosystem, retaining conservative bounded/full fallback tests for unsupported constructs.

findings.impact: A malformed or partially recovered source tree can be asserted to have complete conditional dependency coverage, allowing the consumer to exclude tests despite analysis of an incomplete or incorrect syntax tree.
findings.text: src/impact/node-static.ts certifies tree-sitter trees without rejecting parse errors or missing tokens. A changed commit with `export function a() { return 2;` and no closing brace produces schema v2 conditional with no gap or fallback, although tsc reports TS1005. Reject malformed/recovered trees for both endpoints.

findings.impact: The test suite passes while the analyzer incorrectly reports conditional completeness for syntactically invalid committed inputs.
findings.text: test/impact-conditional-contract.test.ts does not cover missing anonymous syntax tokens or other tree-sitter recovery shapes. Add a real-CLI regression with a missing closing brace (and both endpoints as appropriate) requiring an unbounded gap and full fallback.

output.summary: Both malformed-tree implementation and regression-test findings are resolved.

findings.text: The only selective Go change is always in package A; the import-deletion case changes the consumer itself and accepts its own package tests, so it does not demonstrate that a deleted old cross-package dependency reaches surviving dependents. A hardcoded A-only model or a model omitting old cross-package closure can pass. Add the design-required inverse B case (include B targets and exclude unrelated A/consumer) and a deletion/import-change case that exercises old-revision cross-package dependents or explicitly required fallback.

output.summary: Inverse B selection and deleted A old-graph cross-package cases resolve the prior finding.

spec: Implement conservative impact analysis directly in this Trail-code fork specified in docs/test-impact/design.md, sections 1–6, 8, 11–13 and delivery steps 1–2. Use upstream base ca20a67764e99531a1cf272eea8354e2c16f71d9 and define versioned impact contracts and exact explicit endpoints. Analyze both snapshots, preserve ambiguity and analysis gaps, traverse complete reverse dependencies without arbitrary limits, handle deletions, renames and rebinding, and isolate and validate conservative caches. Report justified fallback scopes instead of silently omitting uncertainty. Include meaningful tests for endpoint semantics, graph completeness, gaps, cache freshness and representative dependency cases. Preserve upstream licensing and document the pinned source. Do not implement a replacement parser or assume normal navigation output is conservative. The full design and its acceptance matrix are binding; resolve open distribution and interface choices through the workflow. Work directly in this fork for a future upstream pull request; no separate test-impact repository or Git subtree. Preserve the separate Unity plugin branch. Where the design refers to a separate fork and adapter distribution, adapt it to this unified repository. Owner scope clarification: Initial release requires explicit committed Git endpoints only, and must work across platforms and filesystems with ordinary Git repositories, without Btrfs, privileged operations, special mounts or subvolumes. Worktree target support is deferred; reject it clearly rather than silently substituting a commit. Use ordinary test-runner execution with a stable-input assumption and a practical target preflight; do not require proof of checkout immutability, mutation monitoring, filesystem snapshots, or isolated checkout. Adapt the original worktree-specific acceptance cases accordingly.
title: Build conservative two-snapshot impact analysis
